EQ_MAX_BANDS.doc: The maximum number of parametric bands a channel EQ may hold — the operator can add up to this many. Generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_EQ_MAX_BANDS`, which `omx_biquad.h` reads (`output-delay-ceiling.test.ts` reads the header): the native lane allocates exactly this many biquad slots per channel and silently clamps above it, so the model, the wire, and the DSP agree by test, not by memory.

ISO_THIRD_OCTAVE_CENTRES_HZ.doc: The standard ISO 266 one-third-octave centre frequencies, 20 Hz–20 kHz (31 bands) — the classic 31-band graphic-EQ layout's centres.

GEQ_BANDS.doc: The graphic EQ's section count: DERIVED from ISO_THIRD_OCTAVE_CENTRES_HZ, never a second literal. Generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_GEQ_BANDS`, which sizes `mix_geq.h`'s section array — its OWN budget, never a claimant on EQ_MAX_BANDS (graphic-eq-31 spec §3, roster ruling 3).

EQ_FREQ_RANGE.doc: The frequency band a parametric band can be dragged across.

EQ_GAIN_RANGE.doc: The parametric-band gain travel, in dB. The ± scalar `clampEqGain` enforces is READ off this (`core/src/eq.ts` derives `EQ_GAIN_LIMIT_DB` from `max`), so the bound is stated once and a surface cannot draw a wider knob than the clamp will honour.

EQ_Q_RANGE.doc: The Q (resonance) extent of a parametric band.

EQ_NOTCH_Q_RANGE.doc: The Q extent of a NOTCH band. Wider than EQ_Q_RANGE on purpose (#116, operator decision): an ultra-narrow surgical cut is the notch shape's whole point — the FBS ring-out pool plants dbx-AFS-style ring killers at Q ≈ 116 (~1/80 octave), inaudible on program yet fatal to a single ringing frequency. Gain-carrying shapes stay bounded at EQ_Q_RANGE — a Q-116 bell is a resonator, not an EQ move.

HPF_FREQ_RANGE.doc: Where the HPF cutoff can sit (low end); mirrors the drawn low-frequency handle.

LPF_FREQ_RANGE.doc: Where the LPF cutoff can sit (high end).
